body: Senegal is the only African country to use fully blue licence plates. A newer Generation 4 version resembles a standard European plate with white background and a blue strip on the left.

A silver or white truck cab is visible in Generation 4 coverage with various region-specific variants. Near Dakar and Thies, a black pickup truck is seen. The car may be blurred, so landscape clues are important.
A Google Car with visible roof rack and right side mirror is unique to Senegal in Generation 3 coverage. Sky rifts are also visible; roof racks and rifts appear in other countries.
Senegal drives on the right, distinguishing it from Kenya (left driving). Other African countries driving right with coverage include Ghana, Nigeria, Rwanda, and Tunisia.
As a former French colony, Senegal uses French infrastructure including bollards, poles, signs, and road lines.
The official and predominant language in Senegal is French. Other sub-Saharan countries with coverage mostly use English, with Rwanda as a minor exception.
Road numbers and distances appear on white kilometre markers with red tops. Typically, the furthest town is the largest.
Most town entry signs in Senegal are white with a thick pink outline and bold black font.
Simple black lamps with solar panels on top are common in Senegal.
Yellow-orange taxis with black fenders are frequently seen.
Senegal coverage map shows most coverage west of Touba, with limited main roads in the east.
Northern Senegal features a flat, arid savannah-desert landscape with sparse, short, faded-coloured trees.
South of The Gambia is lush and green with palm trees near the coast, while coverage near Dakar is green but more low and coastal.
Diourbel is the only Senegal region with extensive rural coverage, featuring sandy roads with sparse trees. Coverage extends to Babou in Thies region. Sand near Touba tends to be grassy.
Northwestern coast has a slightly rolling landscape of vegetated sand dunes.
A dry landscape with slight hills is seen mostly around Bakel, extending south to Nayé.
A greener landscape with larger hills occurs around Kedougou and Mako.
Irrigated rice fields sometimes appear between St Louis and Richard Toll.
A silver Generation 4 car with a long antenna on the front left is seen on many roads, but not beyond the eastern Diourbel border.
The regular Generation 4 white car is mostly found south of The Gambia, the northeastern coast, and a small area between Kaolack and Saly.
Divided highways exist between Dakar and Touba, and Dakar and Saly, showing as yellow roads without numbers on Google Maps. No divided highways exist in Generation 3 coverage.
The N1 runs northeast-east between Tambacounda and Nayé, with a railway parallel to it, south of the road until just before Youpe Amadi, then northward until Bellé.
Hazy coverage with a low sun over an agricultural landscape can be seen on N2 between St. Louis and Richard Toll.
N2 between Richard Toll and Matam traverses a flat desert landscape with sparse trees and bright blue skies; road orientation varies. The sun's height indicates eastward position.
Bright yellow grass patches are distinct along N3, mainly in the Matam Region.
The road northeast from Kedougou to Mali’s border has hazy bushfire coverage with occasional smoke; the road is paved south of Saraya. The car is always blurred.
Sections in the Saloum River Delta show a flat, slightly marshy landscape with low vegetation.
The Kola-Velingara dirt road from Saré Amirou to Badion is recognized by late afternoon to evening coverage, with later times toward the west.
The Forest of Thies features a dry, slightly hilly landscape of brown vegetation and bright orange dirt roads, often seen with haze.

The silver Generation 4 car with a box on the back right of the cab appears on roads between Richard Toll and Louga, N3 between Tiourene and Matam, the dirt road near Mauritanian border from Matam to Gassamberi, and near Diolotène.
The silver Generation 4 car with a stain at the back left of the cab is seen on N2 from Richard Toll to Matam and Bakel to Nayé, and on N1 between Tambacounda and Nayé.

The silver Generation 4 car with a stain at the back left and a dirty roof appears mainly on N1 between Kaffrine and Tambacounda, and N7 between Tambacounda and Kedougou, and between Dahra and Diakhao.
The silver Generation 4 car with a red cloth at the front left is on the eastern road between Ouro Sogui and Bakel.
The white Generation 4 car with the antenna down parallel to the roof travels on N6 between Ziguinchor and Kolda.
The white Generation 4 car with a dirty back is seen north of Kolda, up to Katonfara.
Dakar is the largest and capital city of Senegal, recognizable by its dense urban area and taller modern buildings.
The Great Mosque of Touba is notable for its five tall minarets visible from afar.
